The celempung is a plucked zither used in Javanese gamelan, of the same zither family as the kacapi of Sundanese gamelan, sounding class 314/315/316. The body is about three feet long and stands on four legs; eleven to thirteen pairs of strings are stretched on either side of the soundbox, usually one side tuned to the pelog scale and the other to the slendro, an octave below the siter. The siter of the same family is plucked with the thumbnail and damped with the fingers; the celempung, as an ornamental instrument, plays ornamental figures based on the balungan melody, at the same speed as the gambang. It is common in gamelan siteran and in other gamelan scorings.
切倫蓬琴為爪哇甘美蘭撥弦樂器，與巽他甘美蘭卡恰皮琴相關；名稱「西特」源自荷蘭語「: The celempung is a plucked instrument of Javanese gamelan, related to the kacapi of Sundanese gamelan; the name siter comes from the Dutch citer, which answers to the English zither, while celempung is connected with the Sundanese musical form celempungan. It is not the Sundanese celempung, which is made of bamboo and struck on bamboo strings. Siter and celempung of every size are the characteristic instruments of gamelan siteran and appear in other gamelan scorings as well.
